PUT /items/{id} updates an existing item and returns the updated item or 404
DELETE /items/{id} deletes an item and returns 204 or 404 if not found
All responses include correct Content-Type: application/json headers
Invalid JSON in request bodies returns 400 Bad Request with an error message
Unsupported routes return 404 Not Found
Unsupported methods on valid routes return 405 Method Not Allowed
Basic token authentication via Authorization header — requests without a valid token get 401
Items are stored in a JSON file and loaded on startup
GET /items supports query parameter filtering by any field (e.g. /items?category=books)
Server handles concurrent requests without crashing using threading

A 'switch' command switches between branches
Commits on different branches are tracked independently

A server process accepts client connections on a configurable TCP port specified via --port flag
Clients connect specifying a username via --user flag and a room name via --room flag allowing multiple independent documents
Basic password authentication is required to join a room configured via a server-side JSON config file
The server maintains each room's document and persists it to disk after every confirmed operation
The server implements Operational Transformation to correctly resolve concurrent conflicting insert and delete operations from multiple clients
The client renders a full screen curses TUI showing the document content with line numbers
The document viewport scrolls vertically and horizontally to follow the cursor
Standard cursor movement is supported including arrow keys, Home, End, Page Up, Page Down, and Ctrl+Left and Ctrl+Right for word jumping
Standard editing operations are supported including character insertion, Backspace, Delete, and Enter for newlines
Local edits are immediately reflected in the client display before server acknowledgement using optimistic updates
Remote edits from other users appear in real time with cursor positions correctly transformed
Each connected user's cursor position is shown as a highlighted column marker with their username displayed above it in a distinct color
A status bar at the bottom shows the filename, connected user count, connection status, and current cursor line and column
A sidebar panel shows all currently connected users in the room and their current cursor line number
Python syntax highlighting is applied when the document filename ends in .py coloring keywords, strings, comments, and numbers using curses color pairs
Ctrl+S sends a save request to the server which flushes the document to disk and confirms
Ctrl+F opens an inline search bar that highlights all matches and cycles through them with Enter and Shift+Enter
Ctrl+H opens a find and replace prompt with per-replacement confirmation
Ctrl+L requests an exclusive edit lock on the document preventing other users from editing until the lock is released with Ctrl+L again
Lock requests are queued server-side and granted in FIFO order with all clients notified of lock status changes
Ctrl+Z sends an undo operation to the server which reverses the last operation from this client

All communication uses newline delimited JSON messages over TCP with the following defined message types: connect, ack, operation, cursor_update, lock_request, lock_grant, lock_release, save_request, save_ack, disconnect, error
The server logs all connections, disconnections, operations, lock events, and errors to a timestamped log file
If a client disconnects and reconnects to the same room it receives the full current document state and resumes normally
The server supports at least 10 simultaneous client connections across all rooms without data corruption

Fetches each URL using urllib from the standard library with a configurable timeout
Parses HTML content using html.parser from the standard library
Extracts all anchor href links from each page and adds discovered in-scope URLs to the crawl queue
Normalizes URLs by resolving relative URLs to absolute, stripping fragments, and deduplicating
Fetches and parses robots.txt for each domain before crawling any page on that domain
Obeys Disallow rules and Crawl-delay directives from robots.txt with per-domain rate limiting
Extracts visible text content from HTML stripping all tags, scripts, and style content
Builds an inverted index mapping stemmed terms to the set of documents containing them with term frequency counts
Computes TF-IDF scores for ranking search results across the crawled corpus
Applies basic text normalization including lowercasing, punctuation removal, and stopword filtering
The inverted index is persisted to disk as a JSON file after crawling completes
The index can be loaded from disk without recrawling via --load-index flag pointing to an existing index file
A REST API server starts on a configurable port after crawling when --serve flag is provided
GET /search?q=query returns a JSON array of results ranked by TF-IDF score each containing title, url, score, and a text snippet
GET /search?q=query&limit=N limits the number of results returned
GET /stats returns JSON containing total pages crawled, total unique terms indexed, index size in bytes, and crawl duration
GET /crawl triggers a new crawl run asynchronously using the original seed file and returns a JSON object with a job_id
GET /crawl/{job_id} returns the current status and progress of a crawl job including pages crawled so far
Generates a static search.html file in the current directory containing a search box that queries the REST API and renders results dynamically using JavaScript fetch
The HTML interface displays each result with a clickable title link, the URL, the TF-IDF score, and a text snippet with query terms wrapped in bold tags
Handles HTTP errors, connection timeouts, SSL errors, and malformed HTML gracefully logging one error line per failed URL
Detects and skips non-HTML content based on the Content-Type response header
Displays a live crawl progress line in the terminal updating in place showing pages crawled, queued, failed, and current URL
Prints a summary report after crawling showing total pages, total terms, top 10 most linked domains, and elapsed time
